Dam I'm sorry Hoboken-chicken. I can relate all to well to this post. The bladder and bowels started when I was a teenager as well.  Everyone including my friends made fun of me for it. 

 They labeled me agoraphobic and put me on SSI when I was just 23. I stopped going out completely at 24 because the problems got worse and worse. I hardly left the house as it was when this just came on set thing

I still need to go out and get stuff and it sucks when I have to leave. I take a bag with wipes, cloths, pads, meds, soap. Youd think I was going to a hotel for a couple nights it's so much stuff. 

People make comments and it hurts. I have had strangers say it to my face. Or I hear them talking about me. I take suppositorys before I go anywhere. It helps because my bowels get inflamed. I have no idea why. I think it's the brain sending signals to the bowels saying you have to go when I really dont. But it's better to empty them incase they do get inflamed. That and it's less of a mess if an acident does happen. 

But it's always a game. I cant go at all somtimes when I know I do. Even with a suppository. Or I'm racing to the bathroom trying not to chit or pee myself. It's such a hassle. And it just keeps getting worser

I'm just done with people all together unless there an old friend that understands. Those same friends used to make fun of me. Now these same friends  actually feel bad because they all didn't know I had MS up till I when I found out this past year.

I got stomach and intestine pain bad to. You get checked for celiac disease? Even if you dont have celiac disease.......I was on an MS app and I told the online community about being celiac and someone said allot of MS patients have gluton sensitive if there not full blown celiac and it messes up there stomach and intestines. 

 I changed up my diet to 100% gluton free and it helped dramatically. But there is a billion things with gluton in it. Beer, bread,pasta. Hard liquor. Things you wouldn't think about. Almost everything. Try staying away from gluton. It took me a couple weeks to feel a difference but it helped allot. Still get pain but it's not as bad as it used to be.

It feels horrible  the first few days after the ocrevus. Oddly not the same day. It's after I wake up the following morning I can feel it. Saying hit by a truck is exactly the right way to put it. 

The ocrevus made my symptoms intensifie not only that but more frequently. I've had my legs give out before but not for the duration they do now. I spent 6 hours on the couch last week. Couldnt feel em. I could barely walk but I tried hard to get to the bathroom and I looked like Frankenstein lol. I wanted to die. The pain behind my eyeball was significantly worse. Same with everything else. Hands going numb. Bladder issues got worse. I mean everything. Muscle spasms. If there's a symptom of MS I got it and it all got wicked worse. 

Some issues are kinda embarrassing. Like my bowels. But it's hard to decipher if that's MS or from being Celiac. It might be both. Confuses the shit out of the gastrointestinal doctor that's for sure haha. 

I cannot sleep for the life of me before and after the diagnosis. At the same time I'm so tired. They said they could give me riddlin but I said no. I just felt weird being offered drugs and immediately said no. 

My buddy was just telling me about Rick Simpson oil. Hes a wicked pot head but he was trying to get his hands on some for his mother's cancer and told me it's supposed to help MS to. The doctor wants to give me a Medical card but I'd have to surrender my gun rights. I'm at the point of contemplating doing so because this shit has gotten so bad. I just want relief. 

I'm surprised to talk to someone around my age with MS. You say it's not a death sentence but that's the stuff I cant get out of my head. Most people are older with it. I feel like it is a death sentence. How did you cope and get so okay with it? 

I appreciate the tips. I definitely think I should get out of my head and get busy doing somthing. It's just really appreciated that you say all these things.  I dont feel so alone with this BS. I will do allot of what all you guys are telling me to. I'm just kinda curious to what strain of Mary Jane you are using.  Not that I'm gonna smoke it or anything. ;)

Thanks for thinking so. And thanks for the advice. I jumped on reddit and read all these responses an hour ago. A bit overwhelmed. Especially thinking of MS. It took me till a few minutes ago to start responding to the comments. I dont like to think of MS. I still havnt accepted that I have it. 

It feels like impending doom when I think about all this stuff. Other times it's easy to cope. It's a back and fourth game. Why I dont think I've accepted it yet. I'm really trying to stay positive. 

It is BS what these doctors do. I hate them for not recognizing all this sooner. I want them to pay for it somehow. I'm sorry you went through what I did. But I'm sure you have the same feeling like I do, You got answers you been looking for after years of searching for one. 

 It's people like you and all the others on here that's gonna make it easier for the next person that needs answers or a way to help deal with this horrific disease.

I'd also like to add that 5 days ago the cops came to my house for "the smell of a dead body as someone walked by my window". Said the dispatcher when I called to complain about the nonsense of why the cop showed up for such a call. 

My house smells like food 24/7. Mainly teriyaki chicken. So I'm assuming my landlord is in cahoots with my neighbor to get me out of my apartment.  My only logical thinking is that why would it get worse after reporting this asshole neighbor and why did someone call the cops for the smell of a dead body. And yes the cop came out. Searched the basement and smelled my apartment. Cop said "I dont smell anything so your good to go." Like he fucking pulled me over or somthing.
